precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”. You cannot have a good understanding if you are not keeping the commandments. It is biblically impossible to understand this Bible while you are not observing the laws of God. There is no way around it. All the foolishness that gets exposed comes from those that refuse to repent and keep God's commandments.

That is why Christ's message from the start was this: “From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.”

So many of our brothers and sisters out in the world have yet to come to grips with what we are here for. Being an Israelite in Christ is not about dressing up as an Israelite. It's not about arguing with white folks in the streets. It's not about flexing your muscles and trying to be a tough guy. And no, it is not about multiple wives.

Being an Israelite in Christ is about observing the Most High God's commandments and faith in his Son, so that we don't die when the Lord returns. The kingdom of heaven is at hand, and you are at risk if you do not repent and seek the kingdom. Point blank, period.

Those who deny Christ and deny keeping the commandments, because they want to fulfil their own lust, come up with absurd breakdowns of scripture. Without repentance there is no good understanding.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.
precepts.point: Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

It begins with fear. That is why at Horeb the Most High gathered the people “that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth”. Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession; fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says. The good understanding belongs to them that do his commandments.

And these are generational commandments: “teach them thy sons, and thy sons’ sons”, children's children, cousins' cousins, so that no generation misses a beat, and the fear that is the beginning of wisdom is taught to the children.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.
precepts.point: Everything is in steps, including wisdom; the fear of the Lord is the first step to being accepted of him, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law and the knowledge of his omnipotency.

note.label: Job 28: Where Shall Wisdom Be Found

precepts.why:
Job asks, “But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?” It is not found in the land of the living; the depth says it is not in me and the sea says it is not with me. It cannot be gotten for gold, nor silver weighed for its price, nor valued with the gold of Ophir, the onyx or the sapphire, “for the price of wisdom is above rubies.” You will not find God's wisdom deep in the roots of Wakanda; there is no price you can give for it.

Here is where it is found: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.” To get the wisdom of the Most High you take heed to his commandments. The fear of the Lord is understanding that the Lord created us, made us, and can take us out, and that fear is the beginning of wisdom. A good understanding is for all they that do his commandments.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and a good understanding have all they that do His commandments, so if you are not keeping the commandments you have no wisdom or understanding.
precepts.point: To deliver their soul from death and to keep them alive in famine. Our soul waited for the Lord, He is our help and our shield, for our heart shall rejoice in Him because we have trusted in His holy name.

note.label: Psalm 33: Rejoice in the Lord O Ye Righteous

precepts.why:
“Behold, the eye of the Lord is upon them that fear him, upon them that hope in his mercy”. What is it to fear him? “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”. Fearing God means you are going to keep the commandments; so if you are keeping the commandments, the eyes of the Lord are upon you. And if you are not keeping the commandments, you have no wisdom or understanding.

This is a heavy psalm. He “beholdeth all the sons of men” and “considereth all their works”, so we need to watch what we do and how we move out here in society. Just because we are not with another brother or sister does not mean we can sneak off and do evil and it will not come up. It will come up.

His eye is on them that fear him “To deliver their soul from death, and to keep them alive in famine.” He is our help and our shield, and our heart rejoices in him because we have trusted in his holy name.

precepts.text: The fear of the Most High is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do His commandments, so if you keep them you should not be afraid but fear the one true Power.
precepts.point: Thou hast trodden down all them that err from Thy statutes, for their deceit is falsehood. Those that err from this Bible, their deceit is falsehood, which is why we have to hate every false way. My flesh trembleth for fear of Thee, and I am afraid of Thy judgments.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.” “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

The fear of the Most High is the beginning of wisdom, and a good understanding have all they that do his commandments. So if you keep them you should not be afraid of the evildoers or of them that err from his statutes, but fear the one true Power. He has trodden down all them that err from his statutes, for their deceit is falsehood, which is why we have to hate every false way.

Those that hope in his mercy are going to keep his commandments. That is why faith without works is dead; you have to have faith and you have to have works. You hope in his mercy and you keep his commandments.

“A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not: but knowledge is easy unto him that understandeth.” How do you get the understanding? “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

You fear the Most High and keep the commandments. The scorner seeks wisdom without the fear of the Lord and cannot find it; the one who does his commandments has a good understanding, and knowledge is easy to him.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; good understanding have all they that do his commandments.
precepts.point: This is why in Ecclesiastes Solomon gives the conclusion of the whole matter: keep the commandments, for that is the whole duty of man.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“Wisdom is before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.” Where does the understanding come from? “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

Understanding comes only through keeping the commandments. The fool’s eyes wander to the ends of the earth because he does not have it. This is why in Ecclesiastes Solomon gives the conclusion of the whole matter: keep the commandments, for that is the whole duty of man.

note.label: The Power Of Hope

Our people are sick out there and need watches in every community; they need God's commandments, and that is what the blitz is about. Some of you do only two blitzes a year, only the local ones. Repent of that spirit and shake that dust.

note.label: Flawed Apologetic Doctrine

precepts.why:
“If thou desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord shall give her unto thee.” If you desire wisdom, the understanding of what God is explaining to us, you keep the commandments. You do not start looking for scriptures to explain why you do not have to keep the law.

Here is the prerequisite. God said he will give it to you, but here is the caveat: you have to keep the commandments. One preacher said that if you keep the commandments you are sinning, and the people sat there and said Praise Jesus. So God inspired these words, then got to the New Testament and threw it all out? That would make God bipolar, and God does not change. When Christ walked the earth there was no New Testament. What was he teaching from? What was Paul referencing?

And what is being fought over? We are telling men to stay home and raise your children, don’t be a deadbeat dad; telling women to stop wearing them pants when you walk out with camel toe and yeast infection. We are trying to help our people, and they are a hard-headed people who do not listen. That is why so many are sitting in prison: they refused to listen.

“For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction: and faith and meekness are his delight.” The Lord wants you to have faith and a meek spirit, a pliable spirit. Before this truth, eating pork, shrimp, smoking weed and multiple women did not seem wrong; once the laws of God were learned, it was: I can’t do that no more. Do I love shrimp and crab more than God? Weed? Multiple women? A choice had to be made, and that is called repentance. That is being born again.

Old people refuse to change and say it does not matter, I’m under grace now, it’s what’s in the inner man. What is in the inner man is an evil man. That is in all of us; we were evil and we have to change. Meekness and faith is a spirit that understands: if I do these things, Lord, I am going to receive the kingdom, so I will humble down and change. The Lord said he will give wisdom, but keep my commandments. Show where that changed in the New Testament.

note.label: Flawed Apologetic Doctrine

precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” It is the same thing read in Ecclesiasticus. The apologetics say the Israelites hopscotch around the Bible. Yes, we do. The Bible tells us to. The Christian church is good at semantic talk and catchy phrases, word soup: it sounds good, but it ain’t saying nothing, and the one who does not know better sits there befuddled and just goes with it.

It shall be given to you, but it begins with you: fear me and keep. God says, I will give you this, but I want obedience. They just want to say, I believe Jesus Christ is Lord, and that is all it takes. Can a wife tell her husband, I believe you’re my husband, and not do the things a husband dictates? That does not make sense. The whole Bible is a book of laws, and then in the New Testament they say we don’t have to keep the commandments.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” The faith is this: if I abide by these commandments and do what you say, God, I will inherit the kingdom of heaven. Knowing that, we do not waver, and that is why we are bold in what we say. Some Israelite camps do not study; a brother who sits among us and studies six months would answer most of what the apologetics come with.

note.label: THE ART OF A DYNAMIC TEACHER

precepts.why:
“Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” Israel was a wise and understanding people because they feared God and kept his commandments.

“For what nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them”, and “what nation is there so great, that hath statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law, which I set before you this day?” That is what made us great, not skin color. The people of Israel in the Bible were people of color, black, brown, different shades of brown, and melanin is a blessing in itself. But we do not teach that you get the kingdom because you are black. That is what they push out there to negate the message. Christianity is the one about race and color: a white Jesus, white prophets, white angels, and everyone in a biblical movie is Caucasian.

What made us great is that we came from great men and women, Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebecca, Jacob, Leah, Rachel, Joseph, descendants who kept the same laws that Moses brought back to us when we came out of Egypt. When people fear what they do not understand, they minimize it, because they cannot explain it or speak against it. That is a heathen tactic, whether Arab or white: the opposition minimizes what is greater than themselves.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

precepts.why:
“He revealeth the deep and secret things”, but unto whom? Only unto his servants, only unto those who fear God and keep his commandments, because the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.

“He knoweth what is in the darkness, and the light dwelleth with him.” We want the Most High to show us that light and keep bringing forth the beautiful meanings out of the Bible. For him to do so, we have to walk in wisdom as our forefather Daniel did.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

precepts.why:
Why did God reveal the deep and secret things unto Daniel? The children here are Daniel and his brethren: “Children in whom was no blemish”, no spiritual blemish or physical blemish, “but well favoured”. They knew how to carry themselves, not only with the Most High but in the midst of the other nations; they were well mannered.

“Skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science”: they were not dumb children; they were educated in every subject, “such as had ability in them to stand in the king’s palace”.

Read Daniel 2:22 again with that: he had no blemish, he was well favoured, he was skilful in wisdom, he had discernment, and more importantly he was applying the laws of God. That is why the deep and secret things were revealed to him.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

precepts.why:
“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.”

One secret was that we are the Israelites. Some of us found that out in the 80s, the 90s and the early 2000s. It was kept from us: when our forefathers got off the first documented slave ship at Jamestown, Virginia, the royal house of David, many of them did not know they were Israelites. That understanding was destroyed from them and taken from them.

Another secret is Leviticus 23, our high holy days. In the world we celebrated Christmas, Thanksgiving, birthdays and Easter, ungodly things taught to us by our oppressors, and thought the feasts were for the so-called white man in Israel posing as a Jew. The Most High said no, those are your high holy days, and he revealed them by sending the prophets before us, the bishops, who gave us the knowledge we have now. And the prophets are only the Israelites.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

precepts.why:
“And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites.” Out of your sons come the prophets: the sons of Judah, Benjamin, Levi, Ephraim, the whole twelve tribes, and nobody else. “Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel?”

If your sons are the true prophets, the opposite of truth is false: the nations are false prophets. Everything we learned came from false prophets, even our kindred brothers in the world who are pastors and ministers, because they teach the doctrine of the other nations, and all the religions that were forced upon us.

points: The Bible is the playing field. The Israelites play from it, and the Christian church and the apologetics allegedly play from it too, so the question is who is lining up the precepts properly. It begins here: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom”.

To fear God is to fear his judgments. The law says thou shalt not commit adultery, and the judgment for it is death, so a man is afraid of that. Christ died for sins, we have a chance of repentance and we are under grace, but grace is supposed to teach us to deny sin. Grace is not a license to sin.

“A good understanding have all they that do his commandments.” If you fear God and keep his commandments, that is how you become wise. The opposite is just as plain: if you are not keeping God’s commandments, you are not wise, and you will not have a good understanding of the scriptures.

So who understands the Bible? Show a scripture, Old or New Testament, of anyone who was not keeping the commandments and yet had the Holy Spirit, understood the Bible and taught it. It is not there. Everyone in the Bible who had understanding, prophet or teacher, kept the laws of God. The sacrificial law is done, the book of Hebrews explains that, but the moral laws stand. So how in 2025 do men believe they do not have to keep the laws and still claim to understand? Men sat and let a preacher spit in their hands and put the spit in their eyes, and passed it off as something godly. Why do they do that? Because they have no understanding.
